question: What is the main feature of a structural heart disorder?

options.A: Infection of the heart muscle from bacterial invasion
options.B: Acute inflammation of the outermost heart lining
options.C: Electrical conduction failure causing sudden cardiac arrest
options.D: Anatomical defects of heart valves, walls, or chambers

explanation: Structural heart disorders involve physical abnormalities in the heart's architecture, such as faulty valves or abnormal walls. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why does the heart undergo structural remodeling during long-term pressure overload?

options.A: To increase the storage capacity for red blood cells
options.B: To prevent electrical impulses from reaching the ventricles
options.C: To preserve cardiac output and overcome increased resistance
options.D: To reduce the overall demand for oxygen in body tissues

explanation: Remodeling is a compensatory change in heart size and wall thickness to handle high workload and maintain blood flow. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h1)

question: What happens in valvular stenosis?

options.A: Infection and scarring of the outer pericardial sac
options.B: Rupture of the chordae tendineae during ventricular systole
options.C: Incomplete closure of the valve causing backward leakage
options.D: Narrowing of the valve opening that restricts blood flow

explanation: Stenosis means narrowing, which prevents the valve from opening properly and obstructs forward blood movement. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the main blood flow change in a patient with mitral regurgitation?

options.A: Complete cessation of electrical conduction in the atria
options.B: Reduced blood supply entering the coronary arteries directly
options.C: Obstruction of blood entering the left ventricle from the lungs
options.D: Backward blood flow into the left atrium during systole

explanation: Mitral regurgitation occurs when the mitral valve fails to seal, leaking blood back into the left atrium when the ventricle contracts. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is part of Tetralogy of Fallot?
explanation: Right ventricular hypertrophy is one of the four classic anatomical abnormalities found in Tetralogy of Fallot. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h3)

question: Where does blood flow in an uncomplicated ventricular septal defect?

options.A: Blood shunts from the left ventricle to the right ventricle
options.B: Pressure in the left ventricle drops significantly below normal
options.C: Unoxygenated blood flows directly into the systemic circulation
options.D: The aorta receives a lower volume of blood during diastole

explanation: Because left ventricular pressure is higher than right ventricular pressure, blood flows across the septal opening from left to right. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which cardiomyopathy features excessive thickening of the heart muscle walls?
explanation: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy involves abnormal muscle growth and thickening, particularly affecting the septum and ventricles. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which phase of the cardiac cycle is hardest for a patient with restrictive cardiomyopathy?

options.C: Closure of the semilunar heart valves

explanation: Stiffened ventricular walls in restrictive cardiomyopathy prevent the chambers from relaxing and filling properly with blood. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h4)

question: What sound is usually heard when blood flows turbulently across a damaged heart valve?
explanation: Turbulent blood flowing through narrowed or leaking valves produces an audible vibration known as a heart murmur. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h5)

question: A patient with advanced heart disease wakes up gasping for air at night. What is this symptom called?
explanation: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea occurs when fluid reabsorbs from tissues into circulation while lying flat, worsening pulmonary congestion during sleep. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which test is the main imaging method used to check heart valve structure?
explanation: Echocardiography uses sound waves to create real-time images of heart valves, wall motion, and blood flow patterns. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of cardiac catheterization in structural heart disease?

options.A: To monitor daily fluctuations in systemic arterial blood pressure
options.B: To evaluate the electrical conduction system pathways across the atria
options.C: To determine the electrical response of the heart to physical exercise
options.D: To measure intracardiac pressures and visualize anatomical defects directly

explanation: Cardiac catheterization provides direct pressure measurements within heart chambers and uses contrast media to map structural abnormalities. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which drug class is mainly used to relieve fluid overload and lung congestion in heart failure?
explanation: Diuretics help the kidneys excrete excess sodium and water, reducing circulating blood volume and easing congestion. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why are anticoagulants often given to patients with severe mitral stenosis?

options.A: To prevent bacterial infections from settling on the damaged valve leaflets
options.B: To prevent blood clots from forming due to sluggish blood flow in the left atrium
options.C: To dilate the narrowed valve opening and improve forward blood movement
options.D: To lower systemic vascular resistance and decrease left ventricular workload

explanation: Stagnant blood pooling in an enlarged left atrium behind a stenotic valve creates a high risk for thrombus formation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is a major difference between a mechanical heart valve and a bioprosthetic valve?

options.A: Mechanical valves are made from animal tissue
options.B: Bioprosthetic valves do not require surgical implantation
options.C: Mechanical valves require lifelong anticoagulation therapy
options.D: Bioprosthetic valves last longer than mechanical valves

explanation: Due to the high risk of blood clots forming on artificial materials, patients with mechanical valves need lifelong blood thinners. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h8)

question: Which procedure uses a catheter with a balloon to open a narrowed heart valve?
explanation: Balloon valvuloplasty uses a catheter threaded to the heart to inflate a balloon, splitting fused valve leaflets and widening the opening. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h8)

question: What critical complication should nurses watch for right after cardiac surgery?
explanation: Accumulation of blood in the pericardial sac can compress the heart postoperatively, causing life-threatening cardiac tamponade. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h9)

question: Why is early use of an incentive spirometer and deep breathing important after open-heart surgery?

options.A: To prevent the formation of deep vein thrombosis in the legs
options.B: To increase blood flow directly through the coronary arteries
options.C: To prevent atelectasis and promote optimal lung expansion
options.D: To decrease heart rate and reduce myocardial oxygen demand

explanation: Deep breathing exercises expand collapsed alveoli, clear secretions, and prevent postoperative pulmonary complications like pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h9)
